text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'dedicated-pool-12' p99 latency SLO breach detected (route: /v1/generate). Current p95=380ms, p99=12.3s, baseline p95=140ms p99=850ms. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/ABCD/dedicated-pool-12?panelId=7 :rotating_light:

Maya (oncall): acknowledged, paging eng-runtime + eng-sre. I'm on it. @Ethan @Rachel can you take a look?

Ethan: looking. grabbing traces and autoscaler logs now. any customer tickets?

CustomerOpsBot: 3 customers (cust-42, cust-gamma, cust-x) seeing increased errors/timeouts in the last 6m. No SLA escalations yet.

Rachel: I see queue depth jump on pool-12 to 4.2k requests, autoscaler target replicas=8, current replicas=6. Autoscaler reports warmup tasks queued.

Ethan: digging into autoscaler logs: 
```
[autoscaler] 2026-03-14T10:09:11Z scale_up request for pool-12 delta=2 reason=queue_depth threshold=1000
[autoscaler] 2026-03-14T10:09:11Z provisioning g4dn.xlarge x2 -> pending (warmup)
[autoscaler] 2026-03-14T10:10:16Z scale_up delayed 65s: insufficient spare capacity in region-us-west-2
[autoscaler] 2026-03-14T10:11:02Z provisioner: instances pending warmup 2
```
Looks like scale-up started but EC2 spin-up + container warmup ~60-90s. That matches the p99 tail.

Jason: infra note: there was a spot reclamation window earlier and capacity pool is fragmented. We have limited immediate spare capacity in us-west-2; provisioning fallback to on-demand should have kicked but never did — investigating why fallback policy didn't run.

Maya (oncall): customer impact? are responses failing or just slow?

CustomerOpsBot: from request logs: 92% success but high latency. Streaming responses are stalling for some clients (chunk gaps >5s). 7% of requests hit client-side timeouts.

Priya: flagging priority: product wants circuit-breaker to avoid client timeouts — but we need live mitigation now. Any quick mitigations?

Ethan: mitigation plan options:
- trigger emergency manual scale to add 2 on-demand instances in us-west-2 (fast but increases cost)
- reduce max_batch_size on busy model variant to lower per-request tail latency (config change, affects throughput)
- route a small % of traffic to hosted fallback model (lower throughput but predictable)
- enable prefix KV cache warmup for recently used contexts (if warmup is the friction)
- throttle low-priority/background routes (reduce queue depth)

Rachel: I can throttle non-critical routes at the ELB level (routes: /embed, /rerank). That should give immediate relief to the generation queues.

Maya (oncall): do manual scale + throttle + route 10% to hosted fallback. Rachel, please start throttling. Jason, can you force the on-demand fallback? Ethan, prepare a config patch to reduce batch_size and enable kv prefetch.

Jason: issuing on-demand trigger now. Command: 
```
infractl provision --pool dedicated-pool-12 --count 2 --type on-demand --reason "incident manual fallback"
```
Output: provisioning started, instances requested. ETA ~80s to in-region readiness.

Rachel: throttling non-critical routes now: set rate limit /embed & /rerank to 10r/s per org. Applied. Queue depth dropped from 4200 -> 2800 in ~30s.

Ethan: pushing runtime config patch to reduce max_batch_size for model 'redwood-alpha-7b' from 64 -> 24 and enable kv_prefetch=true for new nodes. Patching via rollout: 
```
PATCH /runtime/config/pools/dedicated-pool-12
{ "model_settings": { "max_batch_size": 24, "kv_prefetch": true } }
```
Rolling canary to 1 node.

Maya (oncall): good. Set status note for customers. Priya can you draft a short customer update?

Priya: drafting now — short note: "We are aware of increased latency on requests served from dedicated pools in us-west-2. We are mitigating by temporarily throttling non-essential routes, adding on-demand capacity, and shifting a small portion of traffic to our hosted fallback. We'll update in 30m." Sending.

Ethan: can confirm streaming stalls correlate with large batch sizes + warmup mismatch. The runtime keeps a per-connection send buffer; when model GPU is starved (warmup + cold KV cache) chunks take >5s. Smaller batch_size reduces collective scheduling latency.

Rachel: autoscaler logs after manual trigger: 
```
[autoscaler] 2026-03-14T10:12:40Z on-demand fallback provisioning triggered by manual command
[autoscaler] 2026-03-14T10:13:55Z new instance ready -> joining pool
[pool-manager] 2026-03-14T10:14:12Z warmup complete for instance i-0abc123, kv_prefetch applied
```
New instances came up ~150s after initial alert.

Ethan: can everyone check p95/p99 now? Grafana link same.

incident-bot: METRICS SNAPSHOT (10:14:30): p95=165ms, p99=980ms, queue_depth=420 -> 900 -> 320 after throttles and new nodes.

Maya (oncall): big improvement, p99 back under 1s — nice. Any residual customer errors?

CustomerOpsBot: client timeouts reduced from 7% -> 0.7% in last 4m. Two customers reported degraded UX but still functional.

Priya: product notes: we'll schedule an evaluation of autoscaler fallback logic and warmup strategies tomorrow. Need an action item to improve on-demand fallback latency and pre-provisioning heuristics for bursty queues.

Ethan: follow-ups/log tasks:
- autoscaler: add early-on-demand fallback when queue_depth growth rate > X per 10s (Ethan)
- warmup: introduce progressive kv_prefetch on instance spin-up (Ethan)
- runtime: graceful degrade option to drop large-batch scheduling when tail latency crosses threshold (Rachel + Ethan)
- infra: reserve small on-demand buffer or burst capacity in us-west-2 (Jason)
- docs: runbook updates for manual on-demand trigger and throttling steps (Maya/Priya)

Rachel: I'll annotate the incident with timeline and attach traces.

Maya (oncall): closing loop: revert canary change once stabilized? Ethan, how long to keep reduced batch_size?

Ethan: keep it for 30m then slowly roll back to normal batch sizes with monitoring. I'll set an automated regression alert if p99 creeps >1s during rollback.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: p99 returned to <1s and queue depth within normal bounds. Incident duration ~18m. Postmortem required: link https://wiki.redwood.example/incidents/1951234567-hotshot-warmup-lag-slo-breach

Maya (oncall): thanks team. I'll open the postmortem and assign action items. Great quick coordination. :thumbsup:

Rachel: adding runbook notes now.

Priya: customer update sent.

Ethan: filing autoscaler bug ticket and will prototype fallback heuristic.

Jason: I'll propose capacity reservation plan in infra weekly sync.

CustomerOpsBot: customers notified, tracking for follow-up 24h.

Maya (oncall): marking this thread resolved. Good job everyone.
